captions.Instagram:
“Wait — what are all these fees?”

Somebody asks me this almost every week, and it is almost always two weeks before closing.

Closing costs are the most misunderstood number in a home purchase. Not because they’re complicated, but because most people meet them for the first time on a settlement statement three days before they’re supposed to sign. It’s not the cost, it’s the surprise, and most surprises are preventable.

Swipe for three things to know before you get to the closing table. ➡️

The full explainer, plus my free Closing Costs 101 guide: erikakpage.com/closing-costs-101

Erika K. Page | Axen Realty

captions.LinkedIn:
Two buyers can go under contract on the identical house in the identical week and walk into two genuinely different sets of closing costs. That is normal.

What moves the number: the loan type (conventional, FHA, VA and USDA all price differently), the purchase price, the location, the lender, the title company and attorney, and whatever the two sides negotiated.

In Georgia, a licensed attorney conducts your closing, and two government line items on the statement are specific to this state: the real estate transfer tax and the intangible recording tax.

I wrote a plain-English explainer for buyers in Metro Atlanta: what closing costs cover, who typically pays what, and four habits that keep the closing table calm.

gbp.text:
Closing costs in Georgia, explained.

Closing costs are not your down payment. They are the fees required to legally transfer ownership and complete the transaction, and every line on your statement belongs to one of four groups: loan-related fees, title and legal costs, government fees, and prepaid items.

Two of the government line items are specific to Georgia: the real estate transfer tax and the intangible recording tax on your loan. And in Georgia, a licensed attorney conducts your closing.

Read your Loan Estimate the day it arrives, and ask your questions before closing day. It’s not the cost, it’s the surprise, and most surprises are preventable.

The full explainer and the free Closing Costs 101 guide are on my blog. Explanatory only, not tax or legal advice. Erika K. Page, Axen Realty.
